chapter: Yale, Stearns and the big bands
title: Inheriting Collector's Corner from Stearns; collector Hoyt Kline
summary: Stearns handed over the New York news and Collector's Corner column; Avakian gained encyclopedic knowledge of records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: He sure did. Not long after he said, “I think I’ll just keep reviewing records,” which I was sorry to hear him say, because I wanted to get free records. But he said, “Why don’t you do all the other stuff?” Get the New York news to him once a month and write the “Collector’s Corner” column. He said, “At this point in time, you know enough to be able to do it.” He was right. I’d done other things that helped my background in that, but I’ll cover that in a moment. So, having inherited those two things from Marshall, I became more and more involved with record collecting. Of course, with Marshall’s collection I got an encyclopedic knowledge that I couldn’t have gotten anywhere else. I think the only other collector who really had a terrific collection was Hoyte Kline, who lived in Cleveland. He was in the grocery business, quite wealthy. Jerry had looked him up. We all became good friends.
So you really had educated listening too.
